newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Port of Tauranga sees slower trade growth.
newsitem.headline: Port of Tauranga sees slower trade growth.

text.p: The Port of Tauranga Ltd on Monday said it expected further trade growth in the coming year, but at a lesser rate because of pressure on exporters.
Chief executive John Halling said growth would come from increased utilisation of assets, growth in property earnings and general marketing of the Port's services.
Oil products remained the most significant import cargo, rising 10.9 percent to 831,000 tonnes.
The 20 percent profit improvement was driven by increased volumes of a range of cargoes including logs, up 15.8 percent, kiwifruit, apples, steel and containers, chairman Fraser McKenzie said.
"For the first time trade volumes through Tauranga exceeded eight million tonnes," he said.
Exports were up 10.1 percent and imports 5.3 percent.
Total revenues were up 6.7 percent to $39.78 million while property income rose almost 12 percent to $5.26 million, and was expected to grow again this year.
A highlight was the introduction of enhanced shipping services, particularly to Asian destinations, McKenzie said.
